notes: EV Pack is NOT available on Advance, so no heat pump or V2L: fails the hard requirements. Range figures pending final homologation.
Cheapest Ioniq 3 that meets the hard requirements. Premium can only take the EV Pack (not Comfort/Design). GFV for this derivative not yet captured.
The 'everything we'd want' spec: memory seats (Comfort) + Vision Roof (Design; not confirmed to open). £31,445 after grant. Useful as the like-for-like against Kia GT-Line S.

Adds heated front seats/steering wheel, rear vents, reclining rear seats, matrix LEDs, HDA over Premium. Carwow listing says 308mi (likely the Advance figure); Hyundai says 300 for Ultimate. Launched Aug 2026; no owner corpus yet.

picks.note: The rational pick if we don't spend PV5 money. Cash, not the 8.9% PCP.

notes: Only appears via the Richmond £319 PCH offer. Internal V2L on Advance not confirmed.

Tristan's current car. Figures approximate from memory; battery may be 73kWh. Complaints: width and turning circle.

Fails the internal V2L requirement (MY27 spec sheet: internal 3-pin only on N Line S and Ultimate; some dealer pages wrongly say Advance has it). Richmond's expired £279 PCH / 0% PCP were on this trim; a stock MY26 car might differ, so ask for VIN/model year.
Still no internal V2L. 19in wheels cost ~37mi of range.
Meets hard requirements. Sportier trim; Ultimate is £90 cheaper and the one to price.
The Kona trim that matches the brief. Carwow description mentions an electric tilt/slide sunroof. Reviews: double buggy fits in boot; owner family with 2 kids says 95% of boxes ticked.

Internal socket only on GT-Line S; heat pump is an extra-cost option on that grade. List includes heat pump. Brings memory seats and sunroof, so compare against Ioniq 3 Ultimate Comfort/Design/EV (£31,445 after grant) not the bare Ultimate EV.
GT-Line S does NOT get the £1,500 grant that cheaper EV3 trims get; Kia gives a £3,000 PCP contribution instead. List includes heat pump. Kia Finance GFV £20,063.14 (Brayleys example).

Specific car: EMG Cambridge, 27,799 miles, ~4y3m warranty remaining. Listing has a generic-spec disclaimer; confirm heat pump and internal socket on the actual car. Registered before April 2025 so no VED supplement.
List over £50,000 so pays the £440/yr VED expensive-car supplement. Ioniq 5-class charging and width. New-car offer 3.9% + £1,500 contribution.

The 'what I actually want' car: dual powered sliding doors, 360 cameras, ventilated seats. Kia Finance GFV £18,661.50 on 37 months (consistent across RRG and Arnold Clark). Owner complaints: PBV support, infotainment apps, slow software fixes; seats not as modular as an old MPV.

picks.note: Worth it and affordable: seven seats, powered sliding doors, proper V2L.

notes: No V2L: fails the brief. Only here because dealer PCP examples exist for it.
